messages.subject: negbin k distribution in stan and typo (?) in lmgamma function
parts:

Did anybody have experience in implementing negbin k (negative binomial when k=1) in stan.  I was trying to implement using lmgamma function but I assume there is a typo in stan manual: product sign should be replaced with sum sign, gamma function sign with log gamma function sign, 1 - j with j - 1.

Thank you,
Linas

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] negbin k distribution in stan and typo (?) in lmgamma function
parts:
Michael,

Sorry, NEGBIN k is described in "RECENT DEVELOPMENTS IN COUNT DATA MODELLING: THEORY AND APPLICATION" equation (13).

With regards to doc I am confused myself but if we are talking about log then usually we use the summation, 1-j makes the argument negative and gamma function undefined.  Also, since we are talking log I infer that log gamma should be used (similarly to lmgamma).  See the manual section 32.12. Frankly I am not an expert in the multinomial gamma function.

Thank you,
Linas

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] negbin k distribution in stan and typo (?) in lmgamma function
parts:
> On Jun 29, 2015, at 12:55 PM, Linas Mockus <linasm...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Michael,
>
> The negbin k model is attached. Any comments in making it more effective?

Non-centered parameterizations.

I'd also argue for a less extreme indentation and spacing style,
because I find 8 character indents and space before brackets of
all kinds very hard to read.

If you're going to give a parameter a uniform distribution, the
constraints on the declaration need to match (elasticity is
improperly constrained and others may be, too).

real <lower = 0> elasticity;

elasticity ~ uniform (0, 5);

I'd also recommend tighter priors for predictors than

mu_A ~ normal (0, 20);

unless mu_A = -20 or mu_A = 20 are reasonable values.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] negbin k distribution in stan and typo (?) in lmgamma function
parts:
Thanks, Bob. I am concerned about the pow(exp(eta[i]), 1-k) * phi[i]. I
just want to follow your advice of not using exp.

Also, since variance of this model is
Var(Y|x) = E(Y|x) + sigma2*E(Y|x)^(k+1) the phi=1/sigma2. I am not sure
if gamma prior is appropriate. Maybe inverse gamma should be used (or
simply sigma2~cauchy(0,2))?

Since A is around 10 I use A~normal(0,20). Is it better A~normal(0,5) or
similar?

Because of high degree of overdispersion I am trying different models.
Actually my feeling is that there is underdispersion at low means and
overdispersion at large means. Those results are still mentioned in the
5th revision of "Econometric Analysis of Count Data" so hopefully they
still make sense.
Thank you,
Linas
